**Group:** Zooplankton  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A copepod: a small crustacean with a distinctly segmented body — a broader anterior region (cephalothorax) and a narrower, segmented posterior (urosome) — prominent, often long first antennae, jointed appendages, and frequently a single median (naupliar) eye. Females may carry paired egg sacs. Key features: arthropod segmentation, conspicuous antennae, teardrop body tapering to a segmented tail, sometimes egg sacs.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **larvacean** | Larvaceans are soft tadpole-shaped tunicates (trunk plus tail), often in a mucous house; copepods are segmented crustaceans with jointed antennae and appendages. |
| **siphonophore** | Siphonophores are gelatinous colonies of zooids; a copepod is a single segmented animal with appendages. |
